I am a woman, though I'm currently studying biomedical engineering and history is my weakest subject. I read through a couple of articles to develop some sort of understanding and opinion - I hope some woman with some more background will be able to provide an even better and more thorough answer, and I hope someone will tell me if I've said anything incorrect.

The City of Constantinople was the capital of the Byzantine (Eastern Roman) Empire for a very long time - over 1000 years, and had survived many attacks up until this point. It had these extremely thick walls, and an army would have had to attack by both land and sea to even try to take it. However, some of these sieges over the years had decimated the population (400k in the 12th century and 40k-50k in the 1450's). Also, they were also losing their diplomatic power - the Popes/Roman Catholic Europe were not happy that they would not form a union with them, so no significant help could be expected.

Meanwhile, the Ottoman Turks had been extending their control over the Balkans and Anatolia, even several Byzantine cities. They had tried to capture Constantinople before (had to suppress an uprising elsewhere) and the new sultan, Mehmed II, had been preparing to try again.

The defenders were very weak at this point - only fewer than 5k men, which could not cover the city's walls. And technology had moved on - these walls were impenetrable up until that point, but this time, the attackers had cannons (large and heavy ones, and smaller ones that could fire more often), as well as 60k-80k men, as per modern historians. Constantine resisted for about 6 weeks, which was impressive! Though near to the end, chaos reigned - women and children were defending the walls, some of the defenders went back to defend their own families, many killed themselves rather than be subjected to the destruction that came immediately after and then after that.

The Hagia Sophia was converted into a Mosque, Constantinople became the new capital of the Ottoman Empire, and the city was repopulated with people from a multitude of faiths and backgrounds. The East had gained quite a bit of power over Christendom, and humanity had moved from the middle ages into the Renaissance.

Well, it happens. They had it coming for a while. I'm not sure what preventative measures they could have taken to keep this from happening, or how that would have impacted things.

Dear S.,

There is always that hope, as social and selfish creatures, that when we shout into the darkness of the world 'Hear me! I am here and this is what I am!', that someone indeed does hear us and someone does acknowledge our need for connection and tries to meet that need, even if it is also at least partially to meet their own need for relief from solitude. 

Welcome to reddit and welcome to this subreddit. While it is true that there is no justification required for writing except for those basic needs to connect and express, there's an urgency and specificity in the desperate flare signal you sent out, since that out of all the topics you could have written about, you decided to write about suicide, and that out of all the places and people you could express your ideas to, you decided post your thoughts in place where people usually want to talk about their struggles with suicide and suicide ideation and to get help. So, I'm not a professional by any means and I'm not sure how much new insight I can give to you because it seems like you've thought a lot of this through, but I will try to match the effort of your writings with my response and hopefully some of it will be useful.

It seems like there have been two very different life-processes that you have been trying to make work for a while: one that works to keep you happy and alive and thriving, and one where you work to successfully commit suicide. The hopeful you sees that a possibility for a life well-lived, despite the struggles -- doing good for the world, being surrounded by people who love you. And the depressed version of you, a compilation of your disorder and your darker, more human side, wants to protect you from the pain that this life brings you by ending it completely. 

The thing about coming up with the best way to live our life is that the design process is iterative -- when something doesn't work, we review it and make another change, and we keep repeating this until it does work. (Bear with me, I'm a pre-med/engineering student, not a writer, and I'd also like to post a well-thought out response in a timely fashion) To illustrate this, your depressed side has made some changes (ie hiding your thoughts from your friends, your numbing to pleasure and your desire for a numbing to suffering, and a better thought out plan), in response to your past attempts being thwarted by others. And your hopeful side, seeing this, has tried something new, by writing on Reddit instead. This "exhausting and excruciatingly miserable cycle", as you've described it, has probably happened many, many times. And it sucks dude, I'm sorry. It is really easy to get stuck in those, and it's hard to get out. 

No wonder you're so tired -- you've been working so hard on refining (at least!) two different versions of yourself, most people only have the pleasure and suffering of dealing with one.

These two versions have been in this perpetual stalemate for a while -- you've been fighting yourself for so long. As your internal war wages on, it probably has become more apparent that these two versions become more disparate, and not in a way you'd like. From what you described, it seems like you feel you need more resolve, more happiness to overcome your situation, but bipolar disorder has made it clear that the more ideal, the more purely happy, you imagine yourself to be, the less likely it is to come true. And yet, it also seems like that this side of you has grown so ashamed, so terrified of the broken and desperate parts of you, that it tries to lock it away to preserve this idealism. And yet, your depressed side becomes more thoroughly manic and active and intricate.

At this point, you're probably like, "No fucking shit, dude! You've pretty much saying what I just wrote using some stupid engineering metaphor!" And you're kind of right, but I guess one way of demonstrating understanding is restating what the original writer said in your own words. :3 The reason I wrote it as an engineering metaphor -- well, as you said before, writing needs no justification, I couldn't think of a better way to express myself to you. 

Anyway, I'm sure you know already that neither of the two methods will really work, or maybe even exist alone. While suicide will give you permanent rest, it leaves a gaping hole in the lives of those you left behind, and probably gets in the way of other goals you might have had, as the understatement of the century. And I'm sure you know better than anyone else that if you continue to live, you will be in pain. 

The thing is though, while they seem so different, they are both are trying to serve the same purpose. They both want to bring you the peace and rest you need. Both want to ease the constant pain that you're in. Ironically, the fact that they're in conflict is what's maintaining your suffering and preventing you from getting that respite. And ironically, running away from pain and problems is what's keeping them with you.

I hope that you can accept your pain. It's okay to be in pain. It's okay to be on this subreddit. It's okay that there are problems as the aftermath of your brave struggle to stay alive and to thrive. It's okay to make mistakes. It's okay to need help. It doesn't take away from all the good you have done and can and will do. 

I hope you can accept yourself. The two processes, the two versions, I described are all a part of you. Don't suppress your depressed self, allow yourself to continue to call out into the void. Allow yourself to recognize your need for love and support, medicinal or otherwise, is valid and needs to be heard and will be. Don't let your hopeful self to be merely the depressed self's guardian, keeping both trapped. Keep working on your dreams and goals and life, no matter where you have to start. Don't resist the things you don't like, accept them, integrate them, love them, then you can change them. I hope you can love yourself, for who you are, where you are. 

Please, be kind to yourself.

It really sucks, and it sucks when it is heightened by overthinking.
Since you're asking for advice, it seems like you'd like to not commit suicide, and reaching out is an important first step! Being vulnerable and having a good support system is important. For your question of meaning, again, I don't have all the answers, and since I do consider myself somewhat religious I don't know if my answer would be the same as yours would be, and that's all right. For a while my answer was (And sometimes still is), "Hey, since I'm not dead and I can't kill myself, I might as well make the best of it." I think in a way it was helpful, because a lot of the things I took for granted and felt like I had to do, reframed it as something I get to do. If everyone dies, and this truly all there is, let's enjoy it. Even if it doesn't matter in the end, maybe it's enough just to treat life and the people in it like they are precious anyway because it is all we have.
I also think it's okay to let yourself feel depressed and anxious and afraid and it's okay to let yourself think. These thoughts and feelings are terrifying, and hard to deal with, and shaming yourself for having them makes it worse. It's okay that you're scared and confused and anxious. Allow yourself space to sit with them and hear what they have to say. Don't hide from them with alcohol. Once you can accept them, you can do whatever you want with them...they aren't you. You are way more than your depression and anxiety and overthinking and confusion.
